verdict_on_the_asked_question.question: Does putting sanitize_error_message(exc) back into the [hold] log line re-open the leak cleared in round 1?
verdict_on_the_asked_question.answer: NO. The change does not re-open a leak — it strictly NARROWS exposure compared to the pre-change behaviour. Verified empirically, not by reading alone.
why: (1) sanitize_error_message (news_bot.py:242-272) does exactly ONE thing: for each of the 9 names in _SECRET_ENV_NAMES it reads os.getenv(name) and does a literal str.replace(value, '[REDACTED]'). It does NOT call _redact_text and does NOT truncate. On its own it would be insufficient for an arbitrary 402/407 body — it only catches secrets whose EXACT current env value appears verbatim.

(2) But it is NOT on its own. _TokenRedactingFilter is attached at news_bot.py:444 to the ROOT logger (logger-level) AND at news_bot.py:453-454 to every handler already on root — which at that point is the StreamHandler installed by logging.basicConfig at news_bot.py:311. The premise in the task ('only on the anthropic* loggers') is wrong: lines 461-467 add the anthropic/openai/google_genai loggers on TOP of the root attachment, they are not the only attachment. Verified at runtime: logging.getLogger('news_bot').handlers == [] and .propagate == True, and the root StreamHandler carries ['_TokenRedactingFilter']. Handler-level filters run on PROPAGATED records, so _redact_text is a live second layer on this exact line. Already pinned by tests/test_no_token_leak_in_logs.py::test_token_redacted_on_propagated_record_from_arbitrary_child_logger.

(3) Worst realistic payloads, each built through the REAL SDK constructor (openai.OpenAI()._make_status_error_from_response) and pushed through the real classifier + sanitizer + root StreamHandler: 402 OpenRouter 'insufficient credits' body carries no secret material at all; a 401 body echoing the submitted key came out '...for key [REDACTED]' (caught by layer 1 on the exact env value, and would independently be caught by _OPENROUTER_KEY_RE on shape — genuine double coverage); 407 cannot carry the Proxy-Authenticate header at all because openai/_base_client.py:408-427 builds err_msg from response.text ONLY, never from headers.

(4) The proxy-credential worry specifically does NOT materialise on this path. Tested a live proxy failure with HTTPS_PROXY=http://vpnuser:S3cretProxyPw@127.0.0.1:9/ — the SDK raises APIConnectionError whose str() is the fixed literal 'Connection error.', with __cause__ = ConnectError('[Errno 111] Connection refused'). No URL, no credentials, anywhere in the message or the traceback. httpx additionally masks the password in URL __repr__. Credentials travel in the Proxy-Authorization REQUEST header; a 407 RESPONSE carries only a Proxy-Authenticate challenge, which is not client-secret-bearing and is not in the message anyway.

(5) No off-host forwarding. docker-compose.yml pins logging.driver=json-file, max-size 10m, max-file 3 — local rotating files, no syslog/fluentd/gelf driver and no shipping sidecar. grep for addHandler across the whole app returns nothing, so no logging.Handler forwards to Telegram, and no admin ping is built from log text. Per deployment.md:501 the only read path is `ssh root@45.90.216.165 "docker logs hw-news-bot"`.

(6) DECISIVE: the same text was ALREADY being logged before this change, through an identical chain, plus two extra sinks. Pre-change a 402 fell into the bare-APIStatusError catch-all -> ClaudeTranscreationError -> news_bot.py:3152-3156, which logs f'[fallback] ... {type(exc).__name__}: {sanitize_error_message(exc)}' — byte-for-byte the same construction as the new line. AND that per-article branch additionally wrote the sanitized text to pending_articles.last_error, then to failed_articles.last_error (durable SQLite, daily-backed-up per deployment.md:592), and into the [E034] recap that is SENT TO TELEGRAM (news_bot.py:4431-4440 -> admin_alerts.py:445). The hold branch writes to NONE of those (increment_attempt and recap_failures are 'failed'-branch only). So the change moves this text from {rotating local journal + durable backed-up SQLite + off-host Telegram chat} to {rotating local journal} alone.
verdict_on_the_asked_question.conclusion: The redaction chain is sufficient for every payload realistically reachable on this path, and the round-1 A09 finding ('the cause of a hold is recorded nowhere') is now resolved by this line. Keep the line. The two residual items below are hardening, not the leak that was asked about.

findings.category: A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
findings.title: The untrusted upstream error body is written to the journal verbatim and unbounded — nothing in the chain truncates
findings.description:
This is the one genuinely NEW exposure the change introduces, and it is about volume, not secrecy. Neither layer truncates: sanitize_error_message only substitutes env values, _redact_text only substitutes regex matches. Upstream of both, openai/_base_client.py:425 sets `err_msg = err_text or f"Error code: {status}"` — for a NON-JSON body that is the ENTIRE response text, verbatim and uncapped (the JSON branch at :423 is equally uncapped). Measured: a 5,373-char synthetic HTML block page produced a single 5,506-char journal line.

Round 1 this could not bite, because the outage branch dropped the message entirely. It bites now because the hold path is exactly where a large non-JSON body is likely: prod egresses through a sing-box VPN gateway (docker-compose.yml route-setup -> 172.28.0.2) from an RU host that already filters Telegram/Telegra.ph. A captive portal, transparent interceptor or ISP block page is precisely the thing that answers 4xx with a multi-KB HTML document — and if it answers 402/407/408 the row now HOLDS and, per the still-open round-1 finding, is retried every slot forever, re-writing that page each time.

Two consequences. Operationally: json-file rotation is 10 MB x 3, so an oversized recurring line evicts the older entries the operator needs — a self-inflicted forensics loss on the exact failure this change was written to make diagnosable. On the security axis: a vocabulary-based redactor is only as good as the text it sees, and an unbounded blob from an interceptor nobody enumerated is the classic place where a gap in the vocabulary (see the next finding) turns into a real disclosure. Truncation is the generic defence that does not depend on guessing the vocabulary.

The project already treats this as a rule everywhere the text leaves the process — admin_alerts._RECAP_REASON_MAXLEN = 200 for [E034] reasons and _PROMO_TITLE_MAXLEN = 200 for [E035]/[E036]/[E037] titles, the latter explicitly credited to 'audit SEC-PROMO-4'. The log path is the one sink that never got the cap.
findings.location: news_bot.py:3174-3178 (the new [hold] logger.warning); news_bot.py:242-272 (sanitize_error_message — no truncation); news_bot.py:3152-3156 (same gap, pre-existing, on the per-article branch)
findings.impact: A recurring multi-KB upstream error page rotates the 10 MB x 3 journal window down, evicting the diagnostics the [hold] line exists to preserve. Secondarily, arbitrary-length untrusted upstream text passes through a redactor whose coverage is enumerated rather than structural, so anything the vocabulary does not name survives at full length.
findings.recommendation:
Cap it at the sanitize boundary so every caller benefits, matching the existing 200-char convention rather than inventing a new number:

```python
# news_bot.py — module level, next to _SECRET_ENV_NAMES
#: Cap for sanitized exception text written to the journal. Upstream bodies are
#: untrusted and unbounded (openai/_base_client.py:425 puts a non-JSON body into
#: the message verbatim); same idea as admin_alerts._RECAP_REASON_MAXLEN.
_ERROR_MESSAGE_MAXLEN = 500

# in sanitize_error_message, immediately before `return message`:
if len(message) > _ERROR_MESSAGE_MAXLEN:
    message = message[:_ERROR_MESSAGE_MAXLEN] + '…[truncated]'
return message
```
500 keeps a full OpenRouter 402 JSON body intact (measured 217 chars) while bounding an HTML page. Note this is a behaviour change for last_error too — which is the desired direction, that column is backed up daily. Add a case to tests/test_llm_outage_hold.py::test_hold_logs_the_cause asserting a 10 KB body yields a bounded line while '402'/'Insufficient credits' still survive.

findings.category: A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
findings.title: Proxy credentials remain outside the redaction vocabulary — RE-SCOPED DOWN from round 1: confirmed NOT reachable on this path
findings.description:
CORRECTION TO ROUND 1. Round 1 rated this latent and warned that 407 being 'explicitly classified and logged' would put it on a live path. Empirical testing shows that escalation does NOT hold, and the finding is re-scoped accordingly rather than repeated.

What was tested and what it showed: (a) the Proxy-Authenticate header cannot reach the message, because openai/_base_client.py:408-427 constructs err_msg exclusively from response.text and never touches response.headers; (b) a live proxy failure with HTTPS_PROXY=http://vpnuser:S3cretProxyPw@127.0.0.1:9/ produced openai.APIConnectionError whose str() is the fixed literal 'Connection error.' with __cause__ ConnectError('[Errno 111] Connection refused') — the password appeared nowhere in the message, the cause, or the formatted traceback; (c) httpx masks the password component in URL.__repr__ by design. A 407 response body carries a Proxy-Authenticate challenge, never the client's Proxy-Authorization credentials, so a correctly-behaving proxy cannot echo them.

The gap that remains is real but narrower than round 1 stated: I could only make it leak by hand-writing a proxy body that echoes the upstream URL with inline credentials — behaviour no mainstream proxy exhibits. The underlying vocabulary hole is unchanged and confirmed: _SECRET_ENV_NAMES (news_bot.py:229-239) has no HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY entry, and none of the five patterns in _redact_text (news_bot.py:336-366) matches a scheme://user:pass@host shape. No proxy is configured today — re-verified, zero proxy references in Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, .env.example or deploy.sh; egress is a VPN default route, not an HTTP proxy.

It is still worth closing, for one reason: it pairs with the truncation finding above. Once an unbounded untrusted body can reach the journal, the redactor's coverage stops being a theoretical property, and a URL-credential pattern is a one-line structural rule rather than another enumerated secret shape.
findings.location: news_bot.py:229-239 (_SECRET_ENV_NAMES); news_bot.py:336-366 (the five _redact_text patterns); _llm_common.py:84 (the 407 comment that names a proxy topology)
findings.impact: Low and conditional: only if a proxy with inline credentials is configured AND some component echoes the proxy URL into an error string. Verified not to occur through the openai SDK or httpx. Were it to occur via a future dependency, the credential would reach `docker logs hw-news-bot` unredacted.
findings.recommendation:
Unchanged from round 1 and still a two-line fix. Add 'HTTP_PROXY', 'HTTPS_PROXY', 'ALL_PROXY' plus lowercase variants to _SECRET_ENV_NAMES, and add a structural URL-credential rule to _redact_text (order-independent — it cannot collide with the sk- patterns):

```python
_URL_CREDS_RE = re.compile(r"://[^/\s:@]+:[^/\s@]+@")
# in _redact_text, alongside the other .sub calls:
text = _URL_CREDS_RE.sub("://***:***@", text)
```
Per patterns.md the pattern list is a documented contract, so update the order note in the _redact_text docstring in the same commit. Treat as opportunistic hardening, not a blocker for this change.

findings.title: CARRIED FORWARD from round 1, still unaddressed: unbounded head-of-queue hold with no cap and no escalation
findings.description:
NOT re-investigated in round 2 — the scope was the logging question. Recorded here so it is not silently dropped from the consolidated report. Round 1 finding #2 stands unchanged: a hold is unbounded in both time and retries. job() re-reads pending_repo.list_pending()[0] every slot (news_bot.py:4391-4418), 'held' does not strike, there is no max-hold age, and outage_state._compute_next_state goes permanently silent at ping_count >= 3. The diff widens the trigger set to 402/407/408 without adding a bound.

Round 2 adds one interaction worth noting: this is what converts the truncation gap above from a one-off into a recurring write. Because the held row is retried every slot forever, an oversized upstream error body is re-logged 3x/day indefinitely rather than once.

The full argument — including why 408 adds nothing qualitatively new, why 407 is not article-inducible, and why the 402 request-cost band is the real content-correlated case — is in security-auditor-1.json finding #2 and is not repeated here.
findings.location: news_bot.py:4391-4418 (job() re-reads list_pending()[0]); outage_state._compute_next_state (silence at ping_count >= 3)
findings.impact: A single head-of-queue article can stop the channel indefinitely on a condition the bot cannot resolve by itself, with no alerts after the 2h mark, while re-issuing the full 30k-max_tokens request every slot.
findings.recommendation: See security-auditor-1.json finding #2 for the full recommendation (track consecutive holds per link, escalate or rotate past the stuck row, re-ping every 24h instead of going silent).
